question.text: Which of the following is the KEY difference between REIT and InvIT taxation regarding pass-through status?

answer.text: Interest from SPV has pass-through status in REIT but not in InvIT
Dividend from SPV has pass-through status in InvIT but not in REIT
Rental income has pass-through status in REIT but NOT in InvIT; rental income is taxable at the InvIT level
Capital gains on property transfer have pass-through status in InvIT but not in REIT

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook page 282, the tax implications of REITs and InvITs are the same except for pass-through status on rental income. Rental income earned by a REIT is exempt at the REIT level and taxed in the hands of unit-holders (page 278 supports the REIT pass-through rule), whereas rental income earned by an InvIT is taxed in the InvIT's own hands and does not pass through to unit-holders. The Trap: Options A and B reverse the actual treatment of interest and dividend from SPV, which is the same for both vehicles. Option D invents a capital-gains distinction that the source does not draw. Note: Other tax treatments (interest from SPV, dividend from SPV, capital gains) follow the same framework for both REITs and InvITs; only rental income is the source-noted exception.
